Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

latents 1.1.8

Likelihood-ratio tests in compare_models() (2026-10-31)

Results of existing calls are the same as in 1.1.7.

  • compare_models(..., test = "lrt") tests each profile, class or transition model against the one before it, as anova() does, and adds lr_statistic, lr_df and lr_p_value to the comparison table. It answers questions such as: does measurement vary across occasions (lta(measurement = "invariant") against "occasion"), do profiles need their own variances (EEI against VVI), is a pair of indicators locally dependent, does a direct effect or a membership covariate improve fit.
  • The models must be nested, with the same numbers of profiles and group classes; other pairs are refused with latents_bad_nesting. Comparisons across numbers of classes stay with bootstrap_lrt() and get_results(grid, "lmr"), because the chi-square reference does not hold there. Weighted fits are refused with latents_unsupported_weights.
  • Checked against mclust (covariance structures), glca’s gofglca() (a membership covariate) and Mplus 9 (LTA measurement invariance): 27 of 27 quantities agree (equivalence/lrt/).

latents 1.1.7

Local-independence check without advice (2026-10-30)

Results are the same as in 1.1.6.

  • When pairs of indicators are dependent within a class, the diagnostics() check reports the largest pair and its residual only. The advice that followed, “consider local_dependence = or a full covariance model”, named an argument with nothing after it and is removed.

latents 1.1.6

Shorter CRAN check (2026-10-30)

Results are the same as in 1.1.5.

  • Test files taking more than half a second run in continuous integration but not on CRAN. On the Windows builder, 1.1.5 still took 742 s to check.

latents 1.1.5

Seed sensitivity with supplied data (2026-10-30)

  • sensitivity(fit, data = ) on a single-level lpa() or lca() fit dropped every seed with latents_sensitivity_dropped, because the caller’s data lacked the row identifier the fit had added for itself. The supplied data are now numbered the same way, and the result equals the one computed without data.

Shorter CRAN check (2026-10-30)

Results are the same as in 1.1.4.

  • The class enumeration and latent transition analysis vignettes are now articles on the package website, at the same addresses. The package ships the latent profile and latent class vignettes.
  • Regression tests written for earlier reviews, and tests that draw plots, run in continuous integration but not on CRAN.
  • The compare_models() and diagnostics() examples run faster.

latents 1.1.4

Continuous integration (2026-10-30)

No package code changed; every result is the same as in 1.1.3.

  • Comparisons with other packages, run in continuous integration only, allow for reference packages whose results differ between platforms. On Linux under R 4.6.2, multilevLCA and MoEClust gave different answers in three cases, and MoEClust differed between two runs; latents agreed with every other reference package. The mclust noise comparison now checks estimates to the precision that both programs’ stopping rules guarantee.

latents 1.1.3

Zero-weight units keep their classification (2026-10-30)

  • 1.1.2 (a GitHub release) reported the class, uncertainty and posterior probabilities of units with sampling weight zero as NA in assignment, posterior and prediction tables. These units are again reported as in 1.1.1. A unit of weight zero stays out of every count, criterion and starting value, but keeps its row, posterior and assignment in output. Only rows and groups with no observed indicator are left without a class.

latents 1.1.2

Rows without data are no longer assigned a class (2026-10-29)

Estimates, log likelihoods and posterior probabilities used in estimation are unchanged.

  • A row whose every indicator is missing contributes nothing to the fit, so its posterior equals the class proportions. With the default drop_empty = TRUE, such rows already counted for nothing in the sample sizes and classification summaries. The assignment table then gave them the largest class, however. Assignment and posterior tables now keep these rows in their input order, but report their class, uncertainty and probabilities as NA. The same applies to predict() on fitted or new data, lta() assignments, descriptives() by class, sensitivity() agreement and sequence summaries. A group whose rows are all empty has no group class. An empty row in a group with data keeps the group’s class. drop_empty = FALSE keeps the earlier output.
  • A categorical local_dependence pair joins its two items into one. A row could answer only one item of the pair, with no other indicator observed. Such a row was wrongly dropped from the sample sizes, information criteria and classification summaries, and is now counted as observed. Likelihoods are unchanged.
  • predict() for a model with a noise component now refuses a row with only some indicators observed, with condition class latents_unsupported_noise. The fitted noise volume does not define a density for a subset of indicators. A row with every indicator missing is accepted and, like any empty row, reported without a class.

Documentation

  • Rewrote the introductions to the help pages, the bundled dataset descriptions, the package overview (?latents), the DESCRIPTION summary and the opening of the LPA vignette.

latents 1.1.1

Help pages (2026-10-29)

  • S3 methods (print(), summary(), as.data.frame(), plot(), get_results(), parameter_inference() and others for each class) no longer have help entries of their own: the help index has 57 entries instead of 222, and the page for each function says which methods its objects have. The arguments only plot() takes are listed in a section of ?"latents-plots", and ?parameter_inference covers every model family. The topics latents-print, latents-summary and latents-as-data-frame are gone; their content is on ?get_results. No function changed.
  • Clearer descriptions of diagnostics(), get_results(), report(), pool_imputations(), mixture_regression() and bootstrap_lrt(), and of two conditions in ?"latents-conditions".
  • Tests: 112 tests that compare results with other packages, numerical routines, Latent GOLD, published values or independent re-implementations moved from the package tests to tests/equivalence/ in the source repository, where continuous integration runs them. No test was removed.

latents 1.1.0

CRAN release (2026-10-29)

This release brings the changes since CRAN 0.9.21 (the GitHub releases 0.9.22 to 1.0.0) to CRAN. The estimation code is the same as in 1.0.0 and 0.98.1, so every result agrees with those versions. Some results differ from 0.9.21: “Upgrading from CRAN 0.9.21” under 0.98.1 lists when to refit.

  • Tests: the boundary-fit test that uses numDeriv for its standard errors is skipped when numDeriv, a suggested package, is not installed.

latents 1.0.0

Verification against independent programs and published analyses (2026-10-29)

No estimation code has changed since 0.98.1; every result is the same. This release records how each function is verified.

  • Comparisons cover independent model fits, published analyses, component formulas and independent reference implementations. The verification matrix distinguishes these evidence types and counts only complete, agreeing model comparisons toward its independent-source strength. The record, rebuilt from saved results, is equivalence/verification-matrix/VERIFICATION-MATRIX.md in the source repository.
  • New comparisons: Latent GOLD 6.1 (growth mixtures, latent class, profile and transition models, negative-binomial and ordinal mixture regression, and individual fits at one to four classes), glca, randomLCA, BayesLCA, multilevLCA, depmixS4, Rmixmod, EMCluster, mixtools, MoEClust, flexmix, LMest, seqHMM, lcmm, mitml, mitools, and mclust and poLCA for enumeration and the bootstrap LRT; and the published values of SAS PROC FMM, Stata [SEM] Examples 50g and 52g, Masyn (2013), Proust-Lima, Philipps and Liquet (2017), Bartolucci, Pandolfi and Pennoni (2017), Pennoni, Pandolfi and Bartolucci (2024), Benaglia et al. (2009), Grün and Leisch (2008) and the SAS and R blog’s latent class example.
  • Where a reference reaches a different maximum the difference is recorded with its cause. mclust’s default EM tolerance stops up to 0.04 short of the maximum, and the statistics printed in its vignette are that stopping point. The default kmeans start search can return a lower maximum for VVV models with two profiles (banknote, crabs), where search = "emEM" reaches the higher one.
  • Tests: the release-engine comparison of grand-scaled EVV and VVV fits now converges both fits and compares posteriors up to label order (it failed on Linux and Windows), and the poLCA residual statistic is compared to 1e-5.
  • Verification safeguards reject missing comparisons and incomplete result tables. Known-difference exceptions cannot waive parameter-count errors; the LCA wrapper includes the added published HELP reference. The matrix gives no source credit to skipped or errored tests, verifies saved results against runtime-source and result hashes, and excludes internal checks from its external-check headline. All ten new comparison kits have CI jobs that fail on unexpected skips as well as errors and disagreements.

latents 0.98.1

Further release audit repairs (2026-10-28)

  • Equal-variance Gaussian and equal-dispersion negative-binomial mixture regressions again report their residual standard deviations or dispersions and standard errors. Class names on the internal variances had changed the shared parameter’s name, leaving the result-table lookup empty, even with one class.
  • General-engine LTA covariance calculations now differentiate and invert in standardized parameter coordinates for observed, robust and OPG inference. Small outcome units could distort standard errors or cause a false singular-information refusal; large units could also cause that refusal.
  • Zero-weight regression units are excluded from inference transformations and scores, as they already were from fitting. Extreme values on excluded units could otherwise erase standard errors. Additive models normalize their posteriors more stably, so excluded groups with large finite values no longer abort an otherwise valid fit.
  • compare_models() retains every model and its ordering through wrappers forwarding ..., including models named n_profiles, n_group_classes or cutoff. These labels could silently drop a model and change BIC weights.
  • Diagnostics count the noise component as a classification alternative. One Gaussian profile plus noise now receives classification checks instead of being described as having nothing to classify.

Upgrading from CRAN 0.9.21

Refit a model made with 0.9.21 when one of these applies; each is described in full further down.

  • Gaussian indicators recorded in small units (a proportion, metres, a rate). 0.9.21 floored variances at an absolute 1e-6 and stopped EM relative to |log L|: the same data multiplied by 0.001 and by 1e-6 gave log likelihoods 654 and 37,700 below the fit in the original units, with only a boundary warning. Both rules are now unit-free (“Fits that do not depend on the units of the data”), and so are SQUAREM and the quasi-Newton finishes (“SQUAREM and replication in any units”).
  • Occasion labels such as T1 … T10. 0.9.21 ordered them alphabetically (T1, T10, T2, …), so lta() and multilpa(time =) fitted the occasions in the wrong order. Such labels are now refused with latents_bad_time; give the order with factor(levels = ) or zero-pad the numbers.
  • Sampling weights with zeros. A unit of weight zero is now absent from every count, criterion, entropy and start (“Sampling weights”).
  • Several group classes. Start 1 of a multilevel model is now deterministic and can number the classes the other way round (“Class numbering of multilevel models”).
  • ICL, AWE and CLC charge the entropy of the complete classification (“Information criteria”), and EII, EEI and EEE default to search = "emEM" (“Default start search”).
  • Mixture regressions with common = "intercept". The argument had no effect in 0.9.21; it is now refused.

Latent GOLD: mixture regression and sampling weights (2026-10-28)

Mixture regressions (Gaussian, Poisson, logistic; model-based and robust standard errors) and sampling weights in mixture_regression(), lpa(), lta() and two-level multilpa() were compared with Latent GOLD 6.1: 172 estimates, standard errors, log likelihoods and parameter counts, all within its printed rounding (equivalence/latentgold-wider/). The comparison found:

  • coef() of an lta() fit run by the general engine (sampling weights, transition or initial covariates, occasion-varying transitions, second order) returned each continuous mean minus the indicator’s grand mean, the engine’s internal coordinates. It now returns the means in the data’s units, as the profile table always did. vcov(), standard errors and every table were unaffected.
  • mixture_regression() stored its class variances under the names of their positions before the classes were relabelled. No reported number used the names.

Release review (2026-10-27)

A whole-package review confirmed 40 defects. The repairs below each have a regression test; SQUAREM and the replication count are in the next section. The enumeration’s criteria table, which duplicates part of its grid, is kept because 0.9.21 code reads it.

Results that change

  • A latent transition origin that no expected move leaves (an empty row) reported its starting values as estimates and counted them as parameters. Its probabilities are now equal, flagged estimated = FALSE, left out of n_parameters, AIC and BIC (by K - 1 per empty row), and warned with latents_empty_transition_row. Wald inference reports NA for them and keeps the rest of the table, which it used to refuse as singular.
  • A three-step class carried by a single group (or, under vcov_type = "independent", a single unit) reported a standard error of about 1e-16 and a zero-width interval under BCH, proportional and modal assignment, and its pairwise contrasts p = 0. They are now NA, with latents_small_classes.
  • sensitivity() of an lta() fit refits with the fit’s own tol and max_iter; it used lta()’s defaults.
  • Zero-weight units no longer choose the starts or the maximum of a mixture regression or growth mixture, and a level or category seen only on zero-weight rows adds no parameter (regressions, ordinal indicators and local_dependence pairs).
  • An autoregressive growth residual held on its bound reports NA for its standard error and interval, not zero.
  • diagnostics() of a single-level fit, or of a two-level fit with one group class, no longer has the trivial “groups” row in its classification and average-posterior tables, and get_results(fit, "all") follows it.

Refusals and warnings

  • A latent class model with more free parameters than response patterns allow warns latents_unidentified (Goodman, 1974); its estimates are unchanged.
  • confint(), get_results() and summary() of regression, growth and additive fits refuse a level outside (0, 1), which used to give an inverted interval, and refuse arguments they do not take. vcov() warns latents_unused_argument for arguments it ignores, and refuses method = "bootstrap" on covariate fits instead of returning the Wald matrix. summary() of a fit, an enumeration or a bootstrap LRT warns for an argument it ignores (summary(fit, digits = 3) used to do nothing).
  • get_results() refuses an abbreviated table name.
  • More input mistakes raise classed conditions: three-step contracts, unsupported three-step families, and the option checks of multilpa() (latents_bad_argument).

Other changes

  • summary() of a general LTA fit is a result object: read its table with get_results(summary(fit), "table"). Its transition and second-order tables gain an estimated column, and its assignments take the shared layout.
  • coef() and confint() methods for pooled imputations; the intervals are Rubin’s t intervals with each parameter’s degrees of freedom.
  • The default plot of an all-categorical fit with text category labels draws the response probabilities instead of failing.

Known issue

  • A covariate fit stops on the change in log likelihood, which along a flat direction of the logit coefficients cannot place them closer than about 1e-6 to the maximum, and tightening tol does not help. On the equivalence data the coefficients differ from a reference optimiser by 2.6e-6, against standard errors of 0.16 to 0.82. A stop on the score of the coefficients would remove this.

SQUAREM and replication in any units

  • SQUAREM extrapolated on the raw parameters, whose means are in the indicators’ units and variances in their squares, so its step length, and with it the maximum a start reached, depended on the units. With test_anxiety of srl multiplied by 1000 (VVV, four profiles, five starts, seed 3) the fit and its grand-scaled refit differed by 4.92 in log likelihood. SQUAREM now steps in standard-deviation units in multilpa() (and so lpa(), lca() and multilca()), both lta() engines and the additive family, and the two fits agree to 1e-12. Plain EM was already unit-free and is unchanged bit for bit. Accelerated fits can stop at a different iteration and, from some starts, at a different maximum: on the package’s 192 recorded reference fits, 179 log likelihoods moved by less than 1e-6, 9 by up to 1e-4, three rose (by 0.19, 0.84 and 2.29) and one, a short staged fit, fell by 0.0006.
  • The quasi-Newton finish of the general lta() engine (covariates, occasion-specific transitions, weights, mover-stayer, second order) and of growth mixtures stopped relative to |log L|, which a change of units moves, and searched the means in the units of the data. With the indicators multiplied by 0.001, a mover-stayer fit of course_engagement stopped up to 0.028 below the maximum it reaches in the original units. Both now stop on the change per observed value, the general lta() engine searches the means in standard deviations, and the fit is the same in any units.
  • Starts whose log likelihoods are within the fit’s own precision, tol times the number of observed values (the change at which its EM stops), are now treated as tied, and the earliest converged one among them is reported, in every family. The window used to be a relative 1e-10 of |log L|, which a change of units moves and which at |log L| in the thousands spans 4e-7: a weakly separated transition model fitted with tol = 1e-12 reported a start 3.2e-7 below another, a gap depmixS4’s EM then recovered from the reported point. With the default tol = 1e-8 the window is wider than before, so between starts that agree to the precision asked for the earlier one is now reported more often.
  • The additive family’s search for between-group variances at zero compared a derivative with respect to a variance, which has units, with a slack proportional to |log L|. It now compares the derivative in reference-variance units with a slack per observed rating, and accepts a boundary fit within tol per observed rating, as EM stops.
  • Group classes of the additive family that the data cannot tell apart are now flagged as collapsed when setting them equal lowers the log likelihood by less than the replication tolerance, not only when their parameters agree to 1e-8. EM approaches such a pair along a flat ridge and rarely brings it that close: a dispersion fit whose classes differ only in means was flagged from one seed in twelve, and its inference then failed with a singular information instead of the collapsed-class refusal. It is now flagged from every seed tried (latents_weak_class).
  • A start counts as reaching the best log likelihood when it is within 1e-6 times the number of observed values of it, no longer 1e-6 * (1 + |log L|), which moved 40-fold with the units for the same gaps between starts. For data in ordinary units the two are of the same size, so the counts printed for such fits barely change. Every family uses this rule and stores it as replication_tolerance, which sensitivity() reads; the general lta() engine, mixture regressions and growth mixtures did not store one before.

Astra review repairs

  • Zero-weight people no longer determine the covariate coordinates or boundary checks of an LTA fit. Ordinary categorical levels are discovered on positive support; excluded-only categories do not add parameters or change BIC. Unidentified transition coefficients have unavailable bootstrap covariance rows and columns as well as unavailable standard errors.
  • A constant Gaussian response is accepted when its design or offset leaves residual variation. Argument forwarding uses distinct internal bindings and evaluates each supplied expression once, including through multilca().
  • Diagnostics and regression enumeration use the fitted family’s contributing units, sampling weights and classification levels. Newly supported diagnostics families expose the documented entropy and classification tables. Unfinished sensitivity refits remain visible and are not labelled as replicated maxima.
  • Enumeration examples use the current complete-data entropy convention and updated ICL/AWE winners. The full-output equivalence harness checks the new replication likelihood, fails partial output coverage, and runs all reference suites in CI with explicit failures for unavailable dependencies.

Class numbering of multilevel models

  • Start 1 now takes its group classes from Ward’s clustering of the groups’ profile compositions, as its profiles already came from Ward’s clustering, so it no longer depends on the seed. A model with more than one group class can reach the same maximum as in earlier versions with its group classes, and sometimes its profiles, numbered the other way round: the log likelihood and estimates are unchanged, only the labels swap. Scripts that refer to a class by its number should check which class it now is.

diagnostics() as a structured report

  • diagnostics() reports a fit in five domains (estimation, class size, classification, local independence, information), one row per quantity with its value, a status and, where one defines it, its reference: how many starts reached the best log likelihood, starts that failed or did not finish, estimates at a bound, the smallest class, classes with no assigned unit, relative entropy, the lowest average posterior and odds of correct classification, and the bivariate residuals significant at 0.05 after Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment. Values are reported without cut-offs: the published ones (AvePP .70, OCC 5, a 5% smallest class) are rules of thumb, and the package does not impose them. A status marks only facts: a best start that did not converge or a class estimated from less than one unit (fail); failed or unfinished starts, estimates at a bound, a class with no assigned unit, or dependent indicator pairs (check). The print names those first. get_results(diagnostics(fit), "checks") is the table; every value is read from a table the fit already computes, and no estimate changes. as.data.frame() of the result is still the entropy table.
  • diagnostics() now reports on additive, cross-level, mixture-regression and growth-mixture fits, which it used to refuse; a quantity a family cannot support is n/a with the reason. A one-class fit and a class with no assigned unit no longer print NA.
  • Starts that a search screens (short runs by design) are reported apart from finished starts, never as unconverged.

A readable result when it is printed or clicked

  • A fitted latent class model prints its class sizes (and group-class sizes) and a wide table of response probabilities, one row per indicator category and one column per class, rounded to three decimals; it used to print a long table of probabilities and thresholds at full precision.
  • str() of a fit, an enumeration or a diagnostics() result is two lines: the result’s header and where its tables are. A host that shows str() before print() when an object is clicked (Beatrina, RStudio’s Environment pane) used to show some ninety components of internals first. str(unclass(x)) still shows the raw list.

How often the best solution was reached

  • print() of a fit and diagnostics() now say how many starts reached the best log likelihood (“best log likelihood reached by 4 of 10 starts”), and flag a best solution found by a single start. print() used to show the winning start’s index as “best start: 5/10”, which read as a count; the count itself was only in summary(). The numbers are in get_results(fit, "replication") and get_results(diagnostics(fit), "replication").

Clearer refusals

  • Every common input mistake is now refused with a latents_* condition class, no call, and a message that names what is wrong and how to fix it. Of 56 mistakes across the exported verbs, 23 used to raise a bare simpleError; none does now (contract test test-review-1027-error-contract.R).
  • A misspelt, missing or repeated column, and an id listed among vars, each have their own message, with the likely spelling: “vars names Z, which data does not have. Did you mean z?” (the four used to share “Supply at least two rows, unique existing indicators, and one distinct group column.”). The same for id, time, a three-step outcome and descriptives(vars = ).
  • Missing values name the indicators and their counts and point to missing = "fiml"; infinite and NaN values are reported separately, because FIML treats only NA as missing. A non-numeric indicator in a profile model names the column and its class and points to categorical or lca().
  • Passing a fitted model or an enumeration where the data belong now says so by the caller’s own name: “data must be a data frame, but grid is an enumeration result … Pass the data frame the model is to be fitted on.” Passing data where a fitted model belongs raises the new class latents_not_a_fit (also a latents_bad_argument), saying what was passed; parameter_inference(), get_tna() and get_group_tna() gain default methods that do the same instead of R’s “no applicable method”.
  • The plot verbs (plot_diagnostics(), plot_profiles() and the rest) name the object they were given and, for a data frame, say that the plot is drawn from the fitted model itself.
  • candidate_fit() no longer evaluates a call headed by get_candidate’s body with the arguments by value, so its conditions carry no data.

Conditions never carry the data (0.97.4)

  • An error raised while a fitting verb validated its input could carry the whole data set in its call: multilca() forwarded to multilpa() with do.call(), so the recorded call held the data by value, and multilpa() put the setup function’s body (375 lines) at the head of the call it evaluated. R’s own error printing truncates the call, but a host that deparses conditionCall() in full streamed every value of a 400,000-row data set (a 10,000-row object printed as 3.3 MB; now 83 bytes). The fitting verbs now evaluate calls of symbols only (multilpa(), multilca(), lta()), a non data frame is refused with latents_bad_data naming the object’s class, and every candidate error that is stored on a grid or raised again has its call bounded (<data.frame[400000 x 9]> in place of the values).

Third pass: interactions (2026-10-27)

  • A plain categorical item whose labels happen to contain :: is no longer read as a half-observed joined item (the one-class log likelihood was 47.8 too high); only a declared local_dependence pair carries that meaning.
  • compare_models() again accepts fits named n_profiles, n_group_classes or cutoff, as 0.9.21 did; numeric values keep their filtering meaning.
  • A positive sampling weight whose ratio underflows stays a present unit.
  • Regression, growth and additive fits apply the sampling-weight convention to their entropy, average posteriors and classification tables; the two-level regression ICL charges the joint classification entropy.
  • Covariate inference keeps half-observed pair rows; zero-weight outcomes no longer set a Gaussian floor or a growth coordinate; the regression floor stays relative below machine epsilon; a random-intercept growth model whose every person has one observation is refused as latents_not_identified; Brownian residual bounds and starts follow the time units.

Second review of every formula (2026-10-26, round 2)

  • Standard errors of centred fits. Under centering = "grand" or scaling = "grand" the Wald standard errors treated the centring constants as known and were 22-31% too small; they are now estimated jointly (the centring equations are stacked into the information) and calibrate to within 10% in simulation. Under person centring or scaling the observed information is too small by construction, so such fits now default to vcov_type = "robust" and refuse "observed" and "opg"; the robust sandwich, which used to be refused as rank deficient, is correct there.
  • Information criteria. ICL, AWE and CLC charge the soft entropy of the complete-data classification (group classes and profiles) under both conventions; the conventions differ only in the sample size. Under the old rule the “groups” convention charged only the group-class entropy, which is zero for every single-level fit, so icl_groups equalled BIC and clc_groups always chose the largest model. Transition fits keep one entropy per level. Fits with several group classes saved by 0.97.1 report NA for these three until refitted. KIC is documented as −2L + 3(q + 1), the form tidyLPA computes.
  • Sampling weights. Every classification estimate (entropy sum of the criteria, relative entropy, average posteriors, odds of correct classification, the classification-error matrix and the BCH weights) uses the sampling-weighted posteriors; modal counts stay counts. Units of weight zero are absent from every count, estimate, start, refusal and warning in every family, including the cross-level fits (whose restricted log likelihood was inflated by 19/15 with zero-weight groups), grand centring and scaling, and drop_empty = FALSE.
  • A half-observed categorical pair (one item of a local_dependence pair missing) now contributes its observed item under missing = "fiml"; it used to be dropped, which biased the estimates under MAR. The latents_partial_pair warning is no longer raised. Every pair of indicators now has a row in get_results(x, "residuals"); ordinal indicators enter the categorical table, and mixed or count pairs report an association without a test. The categorical chi-square is documented as conservative.
  • Units and origins. The VEI, EVE and VVE M-steps no longer floor a unitless shape at min_variance; min_variance = NULL (the new default) means 1e-6 times the smallest indicator variance in the fitted units; EM stops on a log-likelihood change of tol times the number of observed values, which does not depend on the units; the membership regression’s Newton step and the separation flag no longer depend on a covariate’s origin; mixture-regression standard errors are origin-free up to shifts of 1e6; growth mixtures standardise their predictors as well as the outcome (time in days, hours or calendar years gives the same fit); lta() covariate designs are fitted on a centred, scaled chart.
  • Shared negative-binomial dispersion (count_dispersion = "equal") is no longer forced to its floor on a local condition (the fit through lta() was 23.5 log-likelihood units low).
  • Bootstrap likelihood-ratio tests take their p-value over the valid replicates and report n_invalid, with a latents_failed_replicates warning; the p-value is NA only when fewer than half the replicates are valid. Under the null a spurious extra class is expected to separate or stall, so an invalid replicate is information, not failure.
  • Smaller: start 1 is deterministic for any number of group classes; covariate and cross-level fits record n_best_replicated; nominal and ordinal fits of the same items can be compared; the r3step() by-group-class table reports NA for a non-positive variance; sensitivity() counts optima by an anchor rule; bootstrap resamples are drawn before any refit; a CSV round trip of the data is accepted by every inference verb; lta() refuses rank-deficient covariate designs and counts only identified logits; person centring together with person scaling refuses data whose every group has fewer than three observations (latents_atomic_groups otherwise); mixture_regression() counts rows of positive weight in the observation nesting and no longer refuses a two-level model with as many groups as row classes.

Fits that do not depend on the units of the data

  • min_variance now defaults to NULL: one millionth of the smallest indicator variance (observed values in rows of positive weight, on the scale fitted), in multilpa(), lta(), fit_staged() and the group-class and cross-level families. The old default was an absolute 1e-6, so data recorded in small units met it in ordinary fits: iris in metres gave a VVV solution whose log likelihood was 1.00 below the centimetre fit, and at x 0.001 VVI and EEE were 414 and 465 below, with only a boundary warning. A number keeps its meaning, and the bound used is stored on the fit. mixture_regression() and growth models already used a relative bound.
  • EM now stops when a step changes the log likelihood by at most tol times the number of observed values, rather than tol * (1 + |log L|), which a change of units moved. Plain EM on overlapping profiles now stops at the same step at units x 1e-6, x 1 and x 1e6 (0.048 standard errors from the maximum); before, it stopped 0.06 to 0.19 standard errors away depending on the units. The reported iterations can differ from earlier versions.
  • The VEI M-step compared a shape sum, which has no units, with min_variance. With indicators whose scales differ by about 1e9 (a rate and a population), every start failed with “EM likelihood decreased”, where mclust fits. The EVE and VVE M-steps had an absolute floor that broke them for data in units of about 1e-9.
  • Under SQUAREM, iterations counts the EM steps kept: a cycle that falls back to plain EM is two steps, not three.
  • centering = "person" with scaling = "person" turns a group with two observations of an indicator into exactly -1/sqrt(2) and 1/sqrt(2), on which a profile can collapse. Such groups now raise latents_atomic_groups, and data in which every group is like that are refused.
  • The scaling documentation now lists correctly which structures grand scaling leaves unchanged (EEI, VEI, EVI, VVI, EEE, VEE, EVV, VVV) and which it changes (EII, VII, EEV, VEV, EVE, VVE).

Cores

  • cores larger than the machine’s core count is capped at that count with a latents_too_many_cores warning. On macOS with Apple’s Accelerate BLAS, and on Windows, each worker is a separate R process holding the package and a copy of the data, so cores = 24 on a ten-core machine started 24 R processes and could exhaust memory.

Parallel seed sensitivity

  • sensitivity() gains a trailing cores argument. The seeds are refitted in parallel, each refit on one core and seeding itself, so the table is identical to cores = 1, for profile, transition and growth fits alike. Before, every refit ran on one core whatever the original fit used.

Classification error and three-step estimators

  • Rows with no observed indicator are no longer counted in the classification error matrix, the BCH weights or any three-step estimator (three_step(), r3step()), as they already were not in entropy, the average posteriors and the information criteria. Such a row’s posterior is the class prior, so it was assigned to the larger class and charged that class with errors: on 120 rows of which 3 were empty, P(assigned 1 | true 2) was 0.025 instead of 5e-5. A group with no observed row is likewise left out at the group level. drop_empty = FALSE keeps every row, as before.

Standard errors

  • A probability on its upper bound (one minus the floor, because every other category of its row is on the floor) has an NA standard error, as the documentation states. In a binary item it was reported as exactly 0, with the interval [1, 1], when it was the last category, and as NA when it was the first.
  • When an item’s last category is on the floor (a category one class never uses), only that probability is held at its bound. The whole row used to be held, so the row’s other probabilities had no standard error, and every other error, the class shares included, was computed as if they were known and came out too small: on poLCA’s gss82 with three classes the share errors were 0.0396, 0.0307 and 0.0348 instead of 0.0521, 0.0462 and 0.0348. The errors no longer depend on the order of the categories.

Sampling weights

  • A unit of sampling weight zero now changes nothing: the weights are scaled to the number of units with a positive weight, and such units are in no sample size, criterion, entropy or classification table, in every family (multilpa(), lta(), the additive family, mixture_regression() and growth mixtures). Adding four zero-weight groups to fifteen used to scale the log likelihood by 19/15 and move BIC from 622.99 to 784.74. nobs() counts units of positive weight, as nobs.glm() does; n_observations and n_groups still count the data, and every row keeps its posterior.

Growth mixtures in any units

  • A growth mixture is now fitted in standard coordinates and mapped back exactly: the outcome is centred and scaled, and so is every column of the class-specific, common and random designs except the intercept. Its estimates, log likelihood, standard errors, posteriors, predicted random effects and predictions no longer depend on the units or origin of the outcome or of the predictors. With the outcome multiplied by 1e-5 a fit used to stop 0.06 standard errors short; with time in days instead of years a random slope’s variance was held at the variance floor, 11.3 log-likelihood units low, and reported converged; time in hours stopped 0.12 standard errors short; and a calendar-year random slope stopped with “EM likelihood decreased”. Outcome scales from 1e-5 to 1e6 (with shifts up to 1e8), and time in days, hours, units of 1e5 or calendar years, now give the same fit to about 1e-11 standard errors.
  • Every growth fit now ends with Newton steps on the analytic score and is judged converged when it is within 1e-4 standard errors of the root, as fits with correlated residuals already were; the quasi-Newton stop alone left fits up to 0.35 standard errors short.
  • min_variance floors each random effect’s conditional variance (given the ones before it) in the standard coordinates, in EM and in the final steps alike, and a random-effect covariance is judged degenerate there, also by the eigenvalues of its correlation matrix. A slope in small time units is no longer flagged degenerate.
  • The class table’s assigned_persons and average_posterior leave out persons of sampling weight zero, like every other count.
  • A multilevel growth mixture’s ICL charges the entropy of the joint classification of clusters and persons. It used to add the persons’ marginal entropies to the clusters’ entropy, which overstated it.
  • parameter_inference() drops the interval of a residual standard deviation only for the class whose variance is held at its floor, not for every class.

Standard errors of mixture regressions

  • Standard errors no longer depend on a predictor’s units or origin. The singularity check and the inverse of the information are taken on its correlation form, and its numerical derivatives step by each parameter’s own standard-error scale. With a calendar-year predictor every standard error used to be NA, even with one class, and the slope’s error moved by 0.2% under a shift of origin. Growth mixtures and the latent-transition three-step share the corrected inverse.

Smaller repairs from the review

  • positive_rows in get_results(x, "gaussian_diagnostics") is the number of rows with a Gaussian value and a positive weight, as documented. It used to count the posteriors that had not underflowed, which for a component with SD 0.01 reported 87 of 300 rows.
  • Additive-family inference and bootstrap_lrt() accept the fitted data with its rows reordered within groups; a changed rating is still refused.
  • r3step() reports NA with a latents_singular_information warning for a coefficient whose variance is not positive, instead of a standard error of 0.
  • The “densities vanished” stop is classed latents_vanished_density.
  • A trajectory three-step check names why a weight column cannot be read.

Refusals

  • enumerate_classes(), enumerate_lpa() and enumerate_lca() raise the data error that multilpa() raises (latents_bad_data, latents_bad_categorical) when every candidate fails with it: a column that does not exist, an indicator that is constant or entirely missing, a text indicator. They used to return a grid of failed cells without a condition. Failures that differ between candidates still appear in the grid.
  • mixture_regression() refuses a Gaussian outcome that takes one value in every row with latents_bad_data and says so. It used to report that every start degenerated and suggest fewer classes or more starts.

Review of 2026-10-26 (numerical and validation defects)

  • Exactly constant indicators and covariates are recognised by their range, not by a computed standard deviation, which is about 1e-17 for a repeated 0.1.
  • Standard errors are kept for category labels containing :, ,, [ or ].
  • A direct-effect covariate constant where its indicator is observed is refused; a 17-digit ordinal label no longer merges categories on redraw; unobserved joint categories keep their labels.
  • EVI/VEI variances of a near-empty profile are no longer floored (a 12% bias); growth models in small units no longer stop 380 log-likelihood units short; ordinal regressions at large predictor scales converge; the negative-binomial dispersion is no longer forced to its floor.
  • Homogeneous and occasion-specific lta() fits of the same data can be compared; person-centred fits accept their data re-read from CSV.

latents 0.97.1

Enumeration on several cores

  • With seed given, enumerate_classes() prepares the candidates of a profile, latent class or transition grid on the workers. Previously all of them were prepared in one process before the workers started; for a large grid this took a long time on one core. Each candidate seeds its own starts, so results are identical to cores = 1. Unseeded grids are still prepared in grid order in the calling process.
  • enumerate_classes() gains a trailing verbose argument. The default, cores > 1, reports the preparation, the fitting of the starts and the finished grid in at most four latents_progress messages, with the elapsed time. Group-class families are not reported.

Clearer reports

  • An enumeration’s print separates candidates that failed to fit from fitted candidates that did not converge. Before, both were reported as “did not converge”.
  • A start whose k-means starting values stop at 100 iterations is recorded as a failed start, with that reason in get_results(fit, "starts"). R’s own k-means warning, which read as though the model had not converged, is no longer passed on.
  • Printed enumeration tables omit the model column when it is empty in every row, as in a latent class grid. get_results() keeps it.
  • odds_correct_classification is Inf for a class classified perfectly (average posterior one to within rounding), instead of NA or a number such as 7e15.
  • The knee documentation cites Satopaa et al. (2011).

Review corrections

  • Plot methods take their 0.9.21 positional arguments again (for example plot(grid, "aic") for family and transition grids, whose plot(grid) still draws every criterion as a panel), and multilpa() keeps its released argument positions, with boundary last. The enumeration summary and get_results() again provide criteria beside best. Released base-graphics style arguments to bootstrap-LRT and pooled plots are accepted with a latents_unused_argument warning; these plots are drawn with ggplot2 and returned.
  • Joined local-dependence items keep their full grid of category combinations, each with an estimated probability, so unobserved combinations are part of the model.
  • Direct-effect slopes are solved on the weighted design rather than its cross-product, which no longer appears singular when the covariates have full rank.
  • The homogeneous transition recursion falls back to the log-space recursion when subnormal transition probabilities would overflow its scaled messages.
  • For a model whose inference provides no per-unit scores, the Vuong-Lo-Mendell-Rubin test is reported as unavailable (a classed latents_invalid_lmr refusal, recorded in the note column) instead of failing with an unclassed error.
  • Parallel workers use the parent’s random number generator kinds, are stopped when a call ends abnormally, and retry a lost task at most once. options(warn = 2) is honoured on every worker backend.

latents 0.97.0

  • enumerate_classes() gains a trailing type argument to request "lca", "lpa" or "lta" explicitly. "lca" treats numeric response codes as categorical; conflicting routing or measurement arguments are refused. type = NULL keeps existing fitting behavior. The resolved type is recorded on the enumeration and shown in its print header; tables are unchanged.
  • A numeric indicator fitted as categorical that has non-integer values or more than ten categories now raises a latents_suspect_categorical warning, once per call: every distinct value is fitted as a category, and a continuous indicator may call for a model with Gaussian indicators.

Faster latent transition models

  • Profile and latent class grids in enumerate_classes() now share the worker pool across candidates and their starts, including both emEM phases. Ordered starting values, selection and finalisation stay in the parent, preserving seeded fits. Membership covariates and joined categorical local-dependence models retain serial starts as candidate tasks; group-class families retain candidate-level parallelism.

  • Lost parallel worker results are retried once with fewer workers instead of discarding the grid. Starts or candidates still lost are recorded as failed, and one latents_worker_lost warning reports losses and recovery. Socket dispatch retains completed chunks; tasks within a broken chunk may be rerun.

  • lta() gains cores for parallel random starts, including emEM screening. Transition grids in enumerate_classes() dynamically schedule individual starts in one worker pool, longest estimated first, without nested workers or waiting for candidate batches. Both emEM screening and finalist runs use the pool. Seeded results are identical to cores = 1.

  • lta() gains acceleration, defaulting to "squarem" as in multilpa(). Fits usually need several times fewer EM steps and can change slightly, at the same or a higher maximum. acceleration = "none" restores the previous fits.

  • The forward-backward recursion of homogeneous transition models runs as matrix products, several times faster per EM step with identical results.

  • enumerate_classes() with time or a group-class family no longer fails every candidate on socket workers (Windows, and macOS with Accelerate BLAS).

Default start search

  • Models whose profiles share one covariance matrix (EII, EEI, EEE) now default to search = "emEM"; all others keep "kmeans". Their results can change, usually to a higher maximum, and fitting takes about twice as long. search = "kmeans" restores the previous fits.

Review corrections

  • General latent transition fits detect covariance eigenvalues at the variance floor, including occasion-specific measurement. Such fits are marked as boundary solutions and refuse Wald inference.
  • Zero-weight units no longer determine the internal Gaussian origin, imputation, clustering geometry or initial measurement parameters in profile, membership-covariate and weighted transition fits. Excluded outliers cannot consume an initial profile or erase supported-row precision. Observation and group mappings are preserved.
  • Gaussian support warnings in ordinary and membership-covariate fits exclude categorical-only and retained empty rows. Cross-level models apply sampling weights and check both the individual and group Gaussian components.
  • get_results(fit, "gaussian_diagnostics") exposes per-component Gaussian membership mass, positive contributing rows, weight effective sample size, standardized variances and covariance eigenvalues, and the absolute boundary status. The narrowest standardized direction is also printed. These are descriptive diagnostics, with no automatic spike cutoff or change to start selection. Normalized membership mass is not an independent sample count; thin-profile warnings are heuristics, not proofs of singularity or nonidentification.
  • Bootstrap inference for fit_staged() repeats the measurement stage’s own search controls before refitting the group-class stage, preserving an explicit emEM pool even when a single supplied start disables screening at stage two.
  • latents_thin_profiles counts the free Gaussian measurement parameters: covariances held at zero and held means are excluded, and held variances do not trigger the warning.
  • In latent transition models, thin-profile warnings use weighted memberships of rows with observed Gaussian indicators. Empty or categorical-only rows cannot hide a thin Gaussian profile, even under drop_empty = FALSE. Occasion-specific measurement is checked separately at each occasion, which the warning identifies. Fitted estimates and classification counts are unchanged.

Start search

  • search = "emEM" (new) finds starts by the emEM search (Biernacki, Celeux & Govaert, 2003): a pool of n_screen starts (five times n_starts by default) is screened by a short EM run each, and the n_starts finalists are run to convergence. A successful first start (Ward or supplied) reserves one finalist slot; the others are ranked by screening likelihood. With n_starts = 1, a valid Ward start is therefore always finalized; a single supplied start skips screening. This existing protection is now documented. The pool begins with the kmeans search’s own starts. search = "kmeans" reproduces the fits of 0.96.1, apart from the corrections listed below. On the start-search benchmark (180 fits), emEM attained the finite above-cutoff reference in 136 fits and the kmeans search in 130. The benchmark’s descriptive cutoff was 0.01 for the smallest standardized variance or covariance eigenvalue; values below it do not prove false classes. On the matched 80 heteroscedastic fits, both searches attained that reference in 40 fits, while emEM returned 25 below-cutoff solutions against 12 for the kmeans search. Retained runs took about twice as long by median time and 1.45 times as long in total.
  • Either search reports the highest likelihood among the finished starts. The new latents_thin_profiles warning fires when a profile with its own variances has Gaussian membership mass below its number of free Gaussian parameters. It prompts inspection of covariance and support diagnostics. The warning is heuristic and the estimate is unchanged.
  • Under emEM, get_results(fit, "starts") lists every start of the pool, with its kind, stage and likelihood after screening, and “Best likelihood replicated” counts the starts that were run to convergence.
  • bootstrap_lrt() refits each model with the search, starts, stopping rule, selection and boundary policy it was fitted with, by default (n_starts, max_iter and tol now default to NULL). Staged and covariate refits keep the pool size too.
  • cores distributes the emEM screening and the finished starts, with identical results.

Corrections found by the feature equivalence suites

  • three_step(method = "ml") runs its EM from a fixed set of starts (Latent GOLD’s proportional start first, the modal means, quantile placements, tail starts and twenty draws from a fixed internal seed) and keeps the highest maximum. One start missed a higher regular maximum for skewed or heavy-tailed outcomes. The result does not depend on, and does not move, the caller’s random seed.
  • three_step(method = "ml") reports NA standard errors, with a latents_small_classes warning, for a class carried by a single unit (by a single group under vcov_type = "cluster"); its sandwich was exactly zero.
  • Covariate fits record their max_iter and tol, so a bootstrap refit repeats them.
  • direct_effects values that are NA, not character, or end in an empty term ("y3 ~ z +") are refused as latents_bad_argument; a trailing + was silently dropped.
  • Reported covariance matrices are exactly symmetric (they could differ by one unit in the last place between the triangles).
  • Bootstrap inference drops, and counts, a resample that misses a category of a categorical or joined item, instead of stopping with an internal error.

latents 0.96.1

Inference and numerical corrections

  • Entirely missing groups under drop_empty = TRUE, and zero-weight units, no longer satisfy robust-inference minimum-unit checks or inflate the number of independent units used for the CR1 correction. The correction is consistent across profile, covariate, transition, additive, regression and growth models where those units are supported.
  • Direct-effect information is evaluated with centered covariates and its full covariance transformed back to the reported origin. Translating a predictor no longer causes a false singular-information error.
  • ML three-step outcomes are fitted and differentiated in centered, scaled coordinates, preserving standard errors when the outcome has a large origin relative to its spread.
  • VLMR calculations retain well-conditioned information coordinates and use an equivalent symmetric eigenvalue calculation. Imhof probabilities handle negative statistics and retain genuine small distribution weights. Comparisons whose reference weights cannot be resolved numerically report unavailable probabilities.
  • Structured covariance updates handle active variance floors with a feasible solver that checks optimality, avoiding numerical failures near a bound while preserving the covariance structure and EM monotonicity.
  • Socket-worker cleanup closes surviving and failed connections separately, preserving the typed parallel-failure error when a worker dies.

Paired indicators and weighted trees

  • Pair preparation rejects generated names that conflict with existing raw columns and applies native categorical validation before joining labels. Distinct numeric categories cannot silently merge during pair creation.
  • Regression and growth trees use the sampling weights of the units their posteriors classify, including row, group and person adapters.
  • The independent mover-stayer equivalence reference uses stable probability normalization, so large initial logits no longer overflow its path sum.

latents 0.96.0

Direct effects

  • multilpa(direct_effects = "y ~ z") lets a covariate move a continuous indicator’s mean by the same amount in every profile (differential item functioning), Latent GOLD’s y <- 1 + Cluster + z. The effects are estimated with the profiles, by a conditional maximization step in EM on centred covariates, have standard errors in parameter_inference(), and are reported by get_results(fit, "direct_effects"). predict(), refits, the bivariate residuals and parametric draws use the covariates. Against Latent GOLD 6.1 the log likelihood, BIC, effect, intercepts, variances and their standard errors agree to every printed digit. Effects on categorical indicators and effects that differ by profile are not yet available.

Compatibility

  • Every call that worked in 0.95.12 gives the same result: the new arguments (local_dependence, direct_effects, three_step(variance = )) come last with defaults that change nothing, and three_step(method = "m") still means "modal"; "ml" is taken by its full name.

Local dependence

  • local_dependence = "item1:item2" in lca(), multilca(), multilpa() and the enumeration functions models a pair of categorical indicators jointly within each class, the class-specific association Latent GOLD fits with item1 <-> item2 | Cluster; the other indicators stay independent given the class. get_results(fit, "local_dependence") gives each class’s joint probabilities beside their values under independence. On simulated data the log likelihood, parameter count, class sizes and item marginals agree with Latent GOLD 6.1 to every printed digit.
  • A pair of continuous indicators, local_dependence = "y1:y2", gets its own covariance within each class while every other covariance stays zero: between local independence (VVI) and a full covariance (VVV). The log likelihood, parameter count, covariances and their standard errors agree with Latent GOLD 6.1 (y1 <-> y2 | Cluster) to every printed digit.
  • compare_models() compares a model with paired items and one without, which are fitted to the same data.

Lo-Mendell-Rubin tests

  • get_results(models, "lmr") reports the Vuong-Lo-Mendell-Rubin (VLMR) and adjusted Lo-Mendell-Rubin (aLMR) tests for every pair of converged candidates of a grid that differ by one profile or one group class, as Latent GOLD computes them: the likelihood-ratio statistic referred to a weighted chi-square distribution whose weights are the eigenvalues of Vuong’s matrix, with p-values by Imhof’s method. On two test cases the statistics, the mean and standard deviation of the reference distribution and the p-values agree with Latent GOLD 6.1 to every printed digit.

Maximum-likelihood three-step distal outcomes

  • three_step(method = "ml") estimates the class means of a distal outcome by maximum likelihood, with the step-one classification errors held fixed (Vermunt 2010; Bakk, Tekle and Vermunt 2013). variance = "varying" (default) or "equal" sets the outcome’s variances; the table adds the estimated variance of each class. Standard errors are the clustered sandwich, and contrast = "pairs" compares the classes, as for the other methods. BCH remains the default, being more robust to non-normal outcomes (Bakk and Vermunt 2016).

latents 0.95.12

Quieter and stricter checks

  • A covariate model no longer passes on the estimation warnings of the one-start base fit it uses to check its input (a variance at its bound, no convergence, failed starts): it checks its own estimate for each of them, so one boundary gave two warnings and now gives one, about the model returned. It now also warns, with latents_small_classes, when one of its own classes has effective membership below one.
  • A named plot function asked for one view (plot_profiles(fit, what = "heatmap", scale = "standardized")) warns with latents_unused_argument about an argument that view does not use, instead of ignoring it without a word. what = "all" stays silent, as each view takes its share.

Faster standard errors

  • parameter_inference() computes the observed information of a profile, class, covariate or transition model once per R session for that fit and its data, and reuses it. The first call takes as long as before; later calls, including those made by plot_profiles(), plot_responses() and get_results() when they draw or tabulate intervals, skip the two score evaluations per parameter. On a two-level model of 20,000 observations with 94 parameters, a repeated call took 0.23 s instead of 13 s. Results are identical to a computation without reuse, and any change to the fit or its data computes the information anew.

latents 0.95.11

Named plot functions on every fitted model

  • plot_profiles(), plot_diagnostics(), plot_prevalence() and plot_transitions() take every fitted model of the package and draw the view of that fit’s own plot() that shows the same quantity: plot_profiles() draws a growth mixture’s "trajectories" (also of a mixture regression with class_level = "group"), another mixture regression’s "fitted" lines, an additive or dispersion fit’s "means", a cross-level fit’s "profiles" and a pooled fit’s "measurement" parameters; plot_diagnostics(what = "posteriors") draws the "posteriors" of growth mixtures and mixture regressions; plot_prevalence() draws a cross-level fit’s "composition" and a pooled fit’s "profile" parameters (each profile’s probability within each group class); plot_transitions() draws a general lta() fit’s transition matrix, as before. what = "all" draws these and names the views it leaves out.
  • Any other combination (for example plot_profiles(what = "bars") on a growth mixture, or plot_diagnostics() on an additive fit) is refused with latents_nothing_to_plot, which is also of class latents_bad_argument (the class of the former refusal), and the message names the views the fit’s plot() offers and the named functions that draw them. An argument the mapped view does not take (for example intervals for a trajectory) is refused by name with latents_bad_argument.
  • For profile, class and transition models nothing changes, except that plot_transitions() on a model without transitions, and a named function whose view the fit’s plot() lacks (for example plot_prevalence() on a transition fit), now raise latents_nothing_to_plot with latents_bad_argument, where they raised one of the two.

One contract for every grid

  • plot_enumeration(), plot_selection() and plot_tree() take every grid the package makes: profile and class grids, transition grids (enumerate_classes(time = )), group-class family grids (enumerate_classes(family = )) and regression grids (enumerate_regressions()). Each grid offers the views its candidates carry. Transition grids draw every view, the tree included. Family grids draw their criteria and classification quality against the number of group classes, and a tree of their group classes for each family; their candidates have no profiles, so the selection views are not drawn. Regression grids draw every view, the tree of their classes included. get_results(x, "tree", ...) returns the shared masses on every grid.
  • A view a grid does not offer is refused with the new condition latents_unsupported_view (also of class latents_bad_argument), whose message gives the reason and the views the grid offers. An unknown criterion of a grid is now also of class latents_bad_argument.
  • plot_views(x) of a grid lists every view of that grid, whether it is offered, and why not.
  • plot() of a transition or family grid draws through the same views. Without what it draws the grid’s summary, AIC, BIC and BIC over individuals as panels of one plot, as plot_enumeration() does (0.9.21 drew BIC alone). The 0.9.21 calls that name a criterion still work: plot(x, what = "aic"), abbreviations such as "bic_i", and criterion =. It also takes "all" and every other view of the grid, and passes combine, labels, mark_minimum, cutoff and using on to plot_enumeration(), which 0.9.21 ignored. The plots have the look of the other grid plots: a criterion in its own panel, the lowest value ringed.
  • Regression grids get plot(), which draws AIC, BIC, SABIC and ICL across the classes, and summary(), which returns their table (as as.data.frame() does). Formerly plot() failed with a base R error and summary() gave the default list summary.
  • The selection views of a class (LCA) grid name the singular “class” instead of “classe”.

Criterion panels

  • A grid whose every candidate has one group class draws each criterion once, under its plain name: the group versions of AWE, ICL and CLC are left out when their individual versions are drawn, since without group classes ICL over groups equals BIC over groups. what = "all" on such a grid draws AIC, KIC, BIC, SABIC, CAIC, AWE, ICL and CLC.

latents 0.95.10

Tree plots

  • plot_tree(), plot(x, what = "tree") and plot_enumeration(x, what = "tree") return one plot per tree, printed one at a time on an interactive screen device; combine = TRUE returns every tree as a panel of one plot, the figure of earlier versions. A class has the colour of the class it matches in the first tree, and the classes of one row have distinct colours. Every band that carries posterior mass is plotted.
  • New arguments choose the trees and rows: n_group_classes, n_profiles and model. A single value of n_profiles compares the solutions with that number of profiles across numbers of group classes. level = "groups" plots how the group classes divide. from = c(3, 3), to = c(4, 3) (or candidates by name) compares two chosen solutions.
  • get_results(x, "tree", ...) returns the shared posterior mass behind any tree, one row per pair of classes, with the same arguments.
  • Trees use the rows and groups the fit counts (drop_empty) and their sampling weights at both levels, as the effective class counts do. A fit with a noise component is refused with latents_unsupported_noise, and a named candidate that did not converge with latents_unconverged. A grid with no tree raises latents_no_tree, also of class latents_nothing_to_plot.
  • plot_enumeration() refuses an argument it does not use with latents_bad_argument.

Documentation

  • New guide, Tree plot.

latents 0.95.9

Documentation

  • The package website links each author’s name to their own website (https://saqr.me, https://sonsoles.me), as the sibling packages’ sites do.

latents 0.95.8

Documentation

  • The vignettes, the guides, the case studies and the README use the named plot functions: plot_profiles() (with what = "bars", "heatmap", "raincloud"), plot_responses(), plot_prevalence(), plot_sequences(), plot_transitions(), plot_diagnostics(), plot_enumeration(), plot_selection() and plot_tree(), in place of plot(x, what = ). The function tables of the enumeration guides list them. The model families without named functions (growth mixtures, trajectory classes, mixture regression, additive and cross-level models) keep plot(x, what = ).
  • The LPA and enumeration vignettes mention cores.
  • Every help page is revised: titles and descriptions now say what each function does and returns, without design rationale or history, and every argument states its default. The revision corrected statements that did not match the code, among them the refusals listed by enumerate_lca(), enumerate_classes(), bootstrap_lrt(), compare_models(), enumerate_regressions(), prior_control() and fit_staged(); the columns of starting_values() under full covariance; the tables offered by get_results() (starting values, ordinal and count tables, diagnostics); when latents_no_group_classes and latents_unsupported_inference are raised; and the default vcov_type of weighted fits.

latents 0.95.7

Bug fixes

  • Line plots of profiles and response probabilities (plot_profiles(), plot_responses()) no longer run long indicator names together: names that cannot sit side by side are turned. The profile labels at the right end get a margin sized to the longest label, so they are no longer cut off when there are many indicators, and they are spaced on the axis as drawn, so lines that end close together keep their labels apart.

latents 0.95.6

New features

  • The named plot functions now cover every view of a fit, grouped by subject so that typing plot_ lists them all, and each group’s what takes "all" to draw every view it has:
    • plot_profiles(x, what = ) adds "bars", "heatmap", "raincloud", "parallel" and "pairs" to the lines (what is its last argument, so existing calls are unchanged);
    • new plot_sequences(x);
    • new plot_selection(x, what = ) for an enumeration: "deltas", "heatmap", "smallest", "trust", "diagnostics", or "all" (default), the same as plot_enumeration(x, what = "selection").
    Each draws exactly what plot(x, what = ) draws.

Bug fixes

  • plot(x, what = "all") and report() left out the heatmap of a model with only categorical indicators, which draws its response probabilities.

latents 0.95.3

New features

  • multilpa(), and so multilca(), lpa() and lca(), take cores to run the random starts of one fit in parallel. The starting values are drawn first, in order, so the fit is identical to cores = 1. Models with membership covariates still run their starts on one core.

Bug fixes

  • multilca() and enumerate_lca() no longer refuse categorical, so a call written for enumerate_classes() or multilpa() (categorical = vars) works as is. Every indicator in vars stays categorical whatever categorical names; a name that is not in vars is still refused.

  • plot(what = "heatmap") on polytomous categorical indicators now draws one panel per profile, with indicators as rows and response categories as columns. The former layout, a block of columns per indicator, ran to indicators x categories columns, so with many indicators the numbers overlapped and the indicator names were cut off. Binary indicators keep their one-column-per-indicator layout.

Documentation

  • The model-selection and class-enumeration guides, the enumeration and evaluation vignettes, the LPA workflow, the README and the help pages of lpa(), enumerate_lpa() and enumerate_classes() describe the degenerate one-observation solution and boundary = "exclude".

latents 0.95.2

Fixes found by Equivalence 2.0, the strengthened external validation.

New features

  • New argument boundary = c("allow", "exclude") in lpa(), multilpa(), enumerate_lpa() and the covariate models. "exclude" sets aside starts with a variance at min_variance: solutions in which a Gaussian profile shrinks around one observation, whose likelihood gain is set by min_variance rather than by the data. The more starts are run, the likelier one finds such a solution: in a simulation study (29 datasets), a 4-profile dataset fitted with 500 starts gave a 5-profile solution with a one-observation profile that made BIC choose 5; with boundary = "exclude" BIC chose 4, as Mplus did. Opt-in: the default ("allow") and every existing result are unchanged. When every start is at the bound, the best is reported with a latents_all_starts_boundary warning. Categorical indicators alone are unaffected.

Bug fixes

  • lta() beyond homogeneous transitions (transitions = "occasion", covariates, second order, mover-stayer) stopped its quasi-Newton finish early near a transition estimated at zero: since 0.9.13 the finish’s stopping rule was tied to tol, and at the default tol = 1e-10 an occasion-specific model of LMest’s reference was left 2.8e-6 below its maximum with transitions 1e-4 off. The finish again runs to L-BFGS-B’s tight rule, as in 0.9.1, and agrees with LMest to 1.7e-6 or better. Fits move closer to their maximum; nothing else changes.
  • r3step() could stop with latents_no_converge when a covariate nearly separates the classes: the likelihood with the classification error held fixed is not concave, and BFGS from zero settled on a separation ridge (Mplus UG example 7.3: -log L 81.7 on the ridge, 62.6 at the maximum). The search now also starts from the proportional-assignment estimate, which is concave and lies in the maximum’s basin, and keeps the better converged end; it reproduces Mplus’s R3STEP estimates.
  • enumerate_classes(cores = ) on macOS with R switched to Apple’s Accelerate (vecLib) BLAS: forked workers died with a segmentation fault once the session had used linear algebra, and the enumeration then stopped with an internal error at printing. Accelerate is not safe in a forked process, so there the candidates are now fitted by a socket cluster, as on Windows; results are identical to cores = 1, as before. Elsewhere the fork is kept.
  • A worker killed by a signal (a crash, out of memory) returned an empty candidate that was not recognized as lost; it now raises latents_parallel_failure, as a worker that fails with an error does, and so does a socket worker that dies.
  • The condition catalogue lists latents_parallel_failure, raised by enumerate_classes(cores = ) when a worker process fails.

Equivalence

  • The external validation now includes 160 simulated datasets with known parameters fitted by Mplus and Latent GOLD (likelihood, parameters, criteria, posteriors, entropy, AvePP, OCC, class counts, group level, predict(), enumeration grids, compare_models(), cores), 42 genuine Mplus runs kept in JStats, scaling against Mplus, sampling weights in a mixture against Mplus WEIGHT with robust standard errors, bootstrap_lrt() against TECH14, and the group-class families at Latent GOLD’s finest quadrature. Comparisons that were scripts now run as tests, and the Latent GOLD kit is compared with the current package rather than with targets saved when it was built. See equivalence/README.md.
  • Every documented claim of agreement with another program or a published result is registered in equivalence/CLAIMS.csv with the test that backs it, and a test fails when a claim or its test changes. Two claims gained tests (bic_rows equals flexmix’s BIC; a noise observation is profile 0, as in mclust’s classification); one was narrowed to what is tested (plain EM follows mclust’s path from the same start).
  • A sabotage battery (equivalence/sabotage/run.R) injects realistic defects into the loaded package and confirms that the tests detect them.

Documentation

  • The class-enumeration guide is rewritten in scientific register, with the methods cited.

latents 0.95.0

Parallel enumeration

  • enumerate_classes(), and through it enumerate_lpa() and enumerate_lca(), gain cores = 1L, which fits the candidates on several processor cores: forked processes on macOS and Linux, a socket cluster on Windows. Every candidate sets and restores its own seed, so with seed given the result is identical to cores = 1 for profile, transition (time) and group-class family grids; only the time differs (a 24-candidate grid of course_engagement took 11.7 s on one core, 4.2 s on four and 3.3 s on eight). Candidates’ warnings and messages are passed on in grid order, with their condition classes. cores = 1, the default, runs as before. parallel, part of R, is now in Imports.

latents 0.9.41

drop_empty

  • multilpa() and lta() gain drop_empty = TRUE, at the end of their signatures; enumerations, lpa(), lca() and covariate fits pass it on through .... It governs what the reported statistics do with rows whose every indicator is missing and groups whose every row is such a row. The estimates and log likelihood are the same either way.
    • TRUE (default): such rows and groups are left out of the sample sizes of the information criteria, of entropy, AvePP and the entropy charge of ICL, AWE and CLC, of the classification tables and plots, and now also of the effective class counts, as Mplus leaves them out. Class counts now agree with Mplus’s counts based on posterior probabilities.
    • FALSE: every number is what latents 0.9.37 reported, so results published with earlier versions can be reproduced (checked against 0.9.37 for enumeration grids, covariate fits, both lta() engines and compare_models()).
  • Fits with different drop_empty are refused by compare_models() and bootstrap_lrt() with latents_incomparable_models.

latents 0.9.40

Groups with nothing observed

  • A group whose every row has every indicator missing is now left out of the group sample size (bic_groups and the other group-convention criteria) and of group-level entropy, AvePP, the classification and entropy tables and the group diagnostic plots, as Mplus leaves it out of its clusters. Its posterior is the group-class prior, not a classification. A group with at least one observed row is unaffected; group class sizes and assignments keep every group. Fits record n_informative_groups. In a single-level fit each row is its own group, so bic_groups now equals bic_individual when rows are empty. Fits without such groups report exactly what they did.

latents 0.9.39

Fixes found by an independent review of 0.9.38, and new references for missing indicators.

Bug fixes

  • compare_models() on a general lta() fit kept rows with nothing observed in the entropy charge of ICL, AWE and CLC; it now uses the rows the fit classified, as every other fit does.
  • predict() failed on a fit with no continuous indicator when it was fitted with scaling, or with centering = "grand"; such a fit is neither centred nor scaled, and now predicts.
  • scaling = "person" judged whether a unit’s standard deviation was zero against the largest value of every unit, so a real but small spread beside much larger values was refused, as was a unit with no observed value of an indicator. Each unit is now judged on its own values, and a unit with nothing observed is left unscaled.

Equivalence

  • Five datasets with different missing-value patterns (missing completely at random, rows with nothing observed, missing at random on an observed indicator, one indicator mostly missing, and a two-level set with empty groups), fitted by genuine Mplus 9 and Latent GOLD 6.1. Log likelihood, sample size, BIC, entropy, AvePP and posteriors agree; the programs’ differing treatment of rows and groups with nothing observed is recorded.

Documentation

  • The model-selection guide describes the choices made before fitting (random starts, centring and scaling, missing values), why entropy and AvePP can disagree, the two levels of classification, and refitting with more starts. The class-enumeration guide points to them.

latents 0.9.38

Scaling of the indicators, group-level diagnostic plots, and classification statistics that leave out rows with nothing observed. Every addition is a new argument at the end of a signature or a new value of what.

Classification quality with missing indicators (bug fix)

  • Under missing = "fiml", a row with every indicator missing was counted in relative entropy, AvePP, the classification and entropy tables, the entropy charge of ICL, AWE and CLC, and the case-level diagnostic plots. Such a row contributes nothing to the likelihood, so its posterior is the prior its group gives it, not a classification; counting it pulled every one of those statistics down (in one example relative entropy from 0.78 to 0.63). They are now taken over the rows with at least one observed indicator, the same rows the individual-level BIC already counted (n_informative). Estimates, log likelihoods and class sizes are unchanged; fits without such rows report exactly what they did. The rows used are kept on the fit as informative.
  • The same rows are now left out of the individual-level BIC of lta() and of covariate fits, which counted every row; multilpa() already did. A covariate fit’s bic_individual therefore agrees with its own get_results(x, "information_criteria"), which it did not when rows were empty. The additive and cross-level families require complete data and are unaffected.
  • The classification-quality and criteria plots of an enumeration labelled each line at its end in every panel, which ran off the edge beside a second panel and overlapped where values were close. With several panels they now share one legend, keyed by colour and shape; a single panel keeps its direct labels, spaced further apart.

Scaling the indicators (scaling)

  • multilpa() gains scaling = c("none", "person", "grand"), at the end of its signature, beside centering. "grand" divides each continuous indicator by its overall standard deviation and "person" by each unit’s own, so centering = "grand", scaling = "grand" fits grand z-scores and centering = "person", scaling = "person" within-person z-scores. It reaches lpa(), the covariate fits and every enumeration through .... The scales are kept on the fit: get_results(x, "data") returns the columns supplied, predict() scales new data the same way, and the bootstrap and staged fits treat a scaled fit as they treat a centred one.
